digest.component_or_area: development process, ticket lifecycle, code review, and commit governance audit
propositions: Current detected_by metadata coverage is 1.1% (7/648 bugs), insufficient to compute escaped-defect rate or detection-stage efficiency; this is the blocking prerequisite for validating quality improvements.

Plan-review first-pass rate is 49.0% with p90 attempts at 8; review-before-claim adoption rose from 29.2% (Q2) to 79.5% (Q3), but 116,560 LLM calls per 4,530 results shows operational load concentration that preflight determinism could reduce.

Completion first-pass is 72.3% overall; Testing-section tickets achieve 79.7% versus 68.6% without, and declared file-impact tickets 74.2% versus 67.6%, indicating textual planning signals correlate with better outcomes but mechanisms remain unclassified.

Code-review first-pass is 97.4%, but caused_by attribution is demonstrably noisy (39 source tickets map to 49 advisory links with visible semantic mixing in fan-in); larger diffs and initial plan non-PASS remain candidate risk signals only.

Source diffs decreased from Q2 to Q3 (median 111.5→95 lines), test co-change increased (84.5→160.5 lines), and process adoption reached ~100% (trailers, DCO, Change-Id) by late August, supporting process maturation but not proven quality causality.

Near-capacity module count is 35 above 720 LOC, 15 above 780 LOC, and 4.09% duplication; 47.7% same-file retouch within 24h identifies hotspots, but true rework, escape causation, and debt impact on cycle time remain unmeasured.
